text: Office workers' blood pressure fell 11 points in a big survey, but only alongside salt cuts. Daily walks lower it.
Coffee apparently boosts memory, though that was only tested on students after a sleepless night.
Three start-up software teams said working from home boosted productivity, but the gain vanished after six months.
A new bridge cut bus commutes by about twenty minutes, compared with a year of major roadworks.
Vitamin D reportedly prevents colds, shown in one supplement-funded winter trial of under-fives.
A reading app helped English-learning children read better than no teaching, but the gains faded by next year.
Pesticides harmed bumblebees: one season in two English counties left colonies with a quarter fewer queens.
An Icelandic public-sector trial found a four-day week with unchanged pay reduced burnout; sick days didn't change.
